Class AlgoAlarmEvaluationService

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.service.AlgoAlarmEvaluationService
@Service public class AlgoAlarmEvaluationService extends Object
Evaluates the configured security alerts and turns the ones that fire into notifications.

All entry points use durable scheduling and freshness checks. evaluateSimpleAlerts(List) runs straight after an intraday price batch and covers the configured alerts on fresh observations. evaluateIndicatorAlerts() runs on a schedule, refreshes stale prices first and covers all six alert types. evaluateAlertsForTenant(Integer) runs both, for one tenant, when a user asks for it.

What each tier evaluates is decided by AlgoAlertScopeResolver, which walks the AlgoTop hierarchy and the standalone alerts and hands back strategy and instrument pairs. Whether a matching condition is worth reporting is decided by AlgoAlertStateService for the types that are specified as crossings, so that a price which is already past its bound when the alert is created stays quiet until it actually moves across. Whether a report has already been made today is decided by AlgoAlarmRecorder through a unique key.

Missing data never becomes a signal. An instrument without a last price, without enough history for its indicator, or without the holding a holding alert measures is logged as unavailable and skipped; it does not fall back to a different measurement and it does not let a zero valued indicator stand in for a real one.

    • evaluateIndicatorAlerts

      public void evaluateIndicatorAlerts()
      Evaluates due background alerts of all six alert types, and the rebalancing of every hierarchy that still owes a plan today.

      Rebalancing runs beside the alert pass rather than inside it. An alert is scheduled per strategy and instrument and can react to a single fresh quote; a rebalancing compares a whole hierarchy against a whole portfolio at one closing date, so it is evaluated once per AlgoTop per day and would gain nothing from the per instrument leases.

    • hasDueAlerts

      public boolean hasDueAlerts()
      Whether any active alert or any rebalancing is due; used before enqueuing background work.

    • evaluateAlertsForTenant

      public void evaluateAlertsForTenant(Integer idTenant)
      Explicit evaluation remains limited to the caller's tenant. Unlike the background pass it also recalculates a rebalancing that already ran today: a user who asks for an evaluation after changing an allocation is not helped by being told to come back tomorrow.
      Parameters:
      idTenant - the tenant whose configuration is evaluated
